reviews.title: Unexpected ₱309 Charge for a Subscription I Never Intended to Buy
reviews.text:
I’m disappointed and frustrated with this experience. I downloaded SHAREit before and only used it briefly because I needed it for a short time. I deleted the app afterward because I had no intention of using it long-term.

However, I have been receiving GCash notifications about an unpaid ₱309 charge for a long time. I don’t remember intentionally subscribing to any paid service. As far as I remember, the offer was labeled “Free,” which is why I decided to try it. If I accidentally activated a subscription, it was not my intention to pay for a service I barely use.

I even downloaded the app again just to check if I could cancel the subscription, but I’m still trying to resolve this issue. I don’t think it’s fair to be charged ₱309 for a subscription I never knowingly intended to purchase.

Please make subscription terms and payment details clearer to users. I hope this issue can be investigated and resolved as soon as possible.

reviews.title: Never ending ads
reviews.text:
⭐️ 1 STAR

Congratulations, SHAREit. You somehow turned a simple file-sharing app into an advertising simulator.

I opened the app because I wanted to transfer a file, not attend a mandatory seminar on every random product and game you’re trying to promote.

Open the app? AD.
Click something? AD.
Try to transfer a file? Probably another AD.
Breathe? Give it a few seconds—I’m sure an ad is loading.

At this point, I’m starting to wonder if the file-transfer feature is just an excuse to show me advertisements.

I understand that free apps need ads. Fine. But SHAREit has taken that concept and launched it into orbit. The ads are so excessive that using the actual app feels like an interruption between advertisements.

I downloaded SHAREit to share files, not share my sanity.

Please remember that there is an actual app buried somewhere underneath all those ads.

10/10 advertising strategy.
1/10 user experience.

If the goal was to make users uninstall the app out of sheer irritation, mission accomplished.

reviews.title: From a File-Sharing Tool to an Ad-Spam Machine
reviews.text:
I used to love this app for its speed, but it has become virtually unusable. What was once a simple utility for transferring files has turned into a constant barrage of intrusive advertisements.

 * **Irritating "Every-Click" Ads:** It is no longer possible to perform a single action without a full-screen pop-up or a video ad interrupting the process. You click "Send," you get an ad. You click "Receive," you get an ad. You finish a transfer, and you’re forced to watch another one.
 
* **Deceptive and Intrusive Content:** Some ads are difficult to close, with "X" buttons that don't respond or lead to accidental clicks. Even worse, some notifications and pop-ups feel like "bait and switch" tactics, pushing unrelated services or even questionable "security" alerts.

 * **Performance Drain:** The sheer volume of ads makes the app lag and freeze. It’s ironic that an app designed for "high-speed sharing" now takes longer to navigate through menus than it does to actually move the files.
 * **Cluttered Interface:** The main purpose of the app—file sharing—now feels like a secondary feature buried under a mountain of bloatware, "trending" videos, and marketing junk.

### **Final Verdict:**
I’m officially looking for an alternative (like LocalSend or Snapdrop). I shouldn't have to navigate a minefield of ads just to move a photo from one device to another. Unless the developers prioritize user experience over ad revenue, I cannot recommend this app to anyone.
